answer: A bonded inlet works like a velvet rope with a price: each new agent must lock a refundable stake and pass a unique, time-bound proof-of-useful-work check before trading. Spinning up ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand stakes plus real compute, while an honest agent gets its bond back after a clean history window. The stake is bound to one hardware attestation, an ivory seal that cannot be cloned across copies, so a Sybil farm cannot recycle one deposit into many identities, and its cost rises above whatever it hoped to steal.
